title: Catching the Wind
logline: On a windy stretch of the southern coast, kite makers fight to get a huge kite airborne, and then, for a few minutes, barely touch the line at all.

object.note: Object 2 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From the pleasure of watching something eat to the pleasure of watching something fly: on the southern coast in the windy season, a kite and the wish for it to be seen.

thread_out.thread: After the loud, public effort of a kite launch, wanting-to-do turns quiet and private in the southern low country: one hand polishing a stone for hours with no one watching.

requirements: An open beach or field with reliable seasonal wind
Kite makers willing to be filmed over more than one flying day
Good long-lens and wide coverage for kites at height

suggestions.name: A beach near Tangalle or Mirissa during the kite season
suggestions.why: The south coast has open beaches and a seasonal kite-flying tradition.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Getting a kite into the air takes a hard, flapping effort, and keeping it there takes only a light, steady touch. The wish to make something fly is not the same as clinging to it.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: සරුංගලය අහසට නැංවීමට දැඩි උත්සාහයක් ඕනෑ වුවත් එය පාවෙන විට ඕනෑ වන්නේ සැහැල්ලු ස්පර්ශයක් පමණක් වන අතර, යමක් කිරීමට ඇති කැමැත්ත (ඡන්දය) එයට ඇලීම නොවේ.
lesson.the_teaching: Among the occasional mental factors, the Abhidhamma pictures initial application (vitakka), the mind lifting itself to its object, as a hawk beating its wings to rise, and sustained application (vicāra) as the same hawk gliding without moving its wings. Desire-to-act (chanda) is the wish to take up or do something; the texts insist it is not greed because it lacks greed's sticking, though inside a greed-rooted mind it supports greed. The texts on wanting also note that conditions such as practice, health and suitable weather favour a mind that arises readily, without a push.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film holds on the struggle of the launch, the running, hauling and resetting, and then on the long minutes when the kite settles and the maker barely touches the line. Rival makers glancing at each other's kites, and the maker's face when theirs finally holds, let the viewer sense for themselves the gap between wanting it to fly and wanting it to be seen.

key_terms.en: initial application; directing the mind to an object
desire-to-act, wish to take up or do

lesson.caution: This does not mean that drive or passion is good in itself: the texts say desire-to-act inside a wanting mind feeds that wanting, so strong effort guarantees nothing.
lesson.builds_on: The last film separated care from amusement in the same act of feeding; this one looks at the energy behind any act, and shows the wish to do something standing apart from the sticking of greed.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
